value.rationale: The sharp negative projection of bounded nonnegative data is a natural stability invariant for quadratic local least-squares approximation on high-dimensional simplices. Exact vertex and barycenter kernels yield two different growth exponents, \(n^2\) and \(\sqrt n\), with explicit constants. Unlike affine projection, which has no barycenter positivity loss, quadratic projection does; the resulting \(n^{3/2}\) contrast is a structural geometric effect rather than an arbitrary computed table or routine increase of a fixed parameter. The scope is pointwise evaluation; no global operator norm is claimed.
